detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` (Pub/Sub logging/metrics) or OTel export from Cloud Ops with the modular input for `gcp:monitoring:timeseries`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Export Cloud Run request, latency, and instance metrics via GCP monitoring sink to Pub/Sub and ingest with `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`, or forward OpenTelemetry from a sidecar/collector if you run hybrid instrumentation. Ensure `service_name` and `revision_name` are extracted. Alert on elevated `server_request_latencies` and `5xx` ratio versus SLO.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="gcp:monitoring:timeseries" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="gcp:monitoring:timeseries"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.40_gcp_cloud_run_task_healt_40"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `gcp:monitoring:timeseries` in `index=cloud` to detect gcp cloud run task health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_40_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Time chart (p95 latency, request rate), Table (service, revision, error rate), Single value (active instances)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` (Pub/Sub logging/metrics) or OTel export from Cloud Ops and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of gcp cloud run task health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
